lesson_title: The General Journal: Repairs in Ink
hook_text: Real accountants never use an eraser. Here's why that makes their books MORE trustworthy.
clip_script: What it NEVER does: erase, paint over, tear out the page. Not because neatness matters, but because TRUST does. A book where numbers can quietly change is a book that proves nothing. So mistakes are fixed IN PEN, with a new entry that reverses exactly the broken piece — dated and explained. The wrong entry stays visible; the correction stands beside it. That is called an audit trail, and it is worth more than perfection — because nobody believes perfect books; everybody believes books that show their own repairs.
visual_style: A ledger page under a spotlight: an eraser approaches and is dramatically rejected; a pen writes the correcting entry beside the error, both glowing as the trail forms.
pacing: Tense build to the rejected eraser, calm authoritative close on the audit trail.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for the classic entries and the surgeon's rule.
